resolution: Fixed the T-junction the user proved with slab screenshots: a selection-scoped Cut landed new vertices on the boundary, but the uncut rim face still spanned that boundary in ONE full-height edge — so the old big edge remained selectable with the strip's short segment z-fighting coincident under it ('the smaller edge on the inside'). The user's phrasing is the spec verbatim: the distance between one vertex to another is the edge. New splitSoupEdgesOnPoints pass in framework/gpu/mesh_edit.zig runs after every parametric cut (basic AND ring): each exact cut point (shared lerp3 guarantees bit-identity with strip points) is inserted into any triangle whose edge runs straight through it — neighbors keep their authored face identity and only gain triangles, so the welded edge graph reads vertex-to-vertex everywhere and the ghost full-length edge disappears. Unit test replicates the exact two-quads-shared-edge scenario; parity harness gains a global no-T-junction probe (no output edge may pass through any output vertex) on all cut/loopcut/mix rows, and the cut rows' S expectation now documents the re-fanned neighbors (3..4). Gate ALL GREEN 17/17 + both zig suites + ship. Committed 4a3298baf, pushed. Host restart picks up this + the full-slice fix (eec813ba8) + level combs (fa0d9edad) together.
